mainEntity.name: How long does immediate loading take compared to delayed loading?

acceptedAnswer.text: Immediate loading provides functional teeth within 24-48 hours of implant placement, whilst delayed loading requires 3-6 months of healing before the final restoration is attached. However, both approaches require similar overall healing times for complete osseointegration, with immediate loading cases needing careful monitoring during the initial months.

mainEntity.name: Are there any risks associated with immediate loading of implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Immediate loading carries slightly higher risks of implant failure if excessive forces disrupt the healing process during osseointegration. Success depends on achieving excellent primary stability, having adequate bone quality, and maintaining strict dietary restrictions. Your dental team will assess whether you're a suitable candidate based on these clinical factors.

mainEntity.name: Can all dental implants be immediately loaded?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not all implants are suitable for immediate loading. This approach requires specific conditions including excellent bone quality, high initial implant stability, and favourable bite relationships. Areas with previous infections, inadequate bone volume, or poor bone quality typically require delayed loading approaches for optimal outcomes.

mainEntity.name: What dietary restrictions apply during immediate loading?

acceptedAnswer.text: Immediate loading protocols typically require soft food diets for the first 6-8 weeks to minimise forces on the healing implant. Hard, chewy, or sticky foods should be avoided, and chewing should focus on areas away from the implant site. Your dental team will provide detailed dietary guidelines specific to your treatment.

mainEntity.name: How do I care for immediately loaded implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Immediate loading cases require gentle cleaning with soft brushes and antimicrobial mouth rinses as directed by your dental team. Avoid aggressive brushing or flossing around the implant site initially, whilst maintaining excellent hygiene in other areas. Regular professional monitoring ensures healing progresses appropriately.

mainEntity.name: What happens if an immediately loaded implant fails?

acceptedAnswer.text: Should an immediately loaded implant fail to integrate, it can typically be removed and the site allowed to heal before attempting replacement. The success rates for replacement implants are generally favourable, though outcomes depend on individual clinical factors and the reasons for initial failure.
